key_insight: In CFD predictions at L/D = 5 and pressure drops above 0.2 MPa, sharp-edged inlets showed strong cavitation while chamfered inlets showed cavitation inception.
engineering_relevance: Inlet geometry and orifice length-to-diameter ratio are important design variables for managing injector cavitation and hydraulic flip.
method: CFD with k-ω SST turbulence, Zwart–Gerber–Belamri cavitation, and Volume of Fluid modeling.
Compared sharp-edged and chamfered inlets over pressure drops of 0.07–0.59 MPa.
Investigated orifice length-to-diameter ratios of 2, 5, and 10.
evidence_signal: Volumetric flow predictions were validated against existing experiments for both inlet types, and hydraulic flip at L/D = 5 and 0.59 MPa for the sharp-edged inlet agreed with prior experimental findings.
watch_item: The abstract reports flow-rate validation but no quantitative error metrics or direct validation of local vapor distributions.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Flow and Cavitation in Single-Liquid Injectors with Sharp-Edged and Chamfered Orifice Inlets
